reviewer: adversarial finder (score not authoritative; see PROMPT-STANDARD "How to review a prompt")

gaps.problem: Item 14 grades `probeVoice` to within 1e-3 against expected values that are derived from the `bandstand` preset's `distance = 70` and `yaw = 2.60` (r = 82, pan divisor 96) - but §8 explicitly grants the builder permission to change exactly those numbers: 'retune the numbers if a shot demands it, keep the intent'. A builder who obeys §8 and moves bandstand to yaw 2.4 or distance 90 to fix a night framing then fails item 14 with a correct positional law, or the critic recomputes from the live preset and the two sides disagree about which table is authoritative. This is the single most likely way this spec costs a round: both halves are individually reasonable instructions that cannot both be followed.
gaps.fix: Make the two constants item 14 depends on non-retunable: in §8 change the permission to 'retune `pitch` and `target` if a shot demands it; `bandstand.distance = 70` and `bandstand.yaw = 2.60` are frozen because item 14's expected values are derived from them.' Alternatively, make item 14 self-anchoring: have the probe read `api.stats()`-adjacent camera state (or `ctx.camera.distance`/`yaw`) into `live.json`, and grade `volume`/`pan` against the formula evaluated at the reported camera rather than against a hard-coded table.

gaps.problem: Item 23 requires '>= 4 distinct pools of L >= 110 on ground or path, each >= 350 px, adjacent to lamp geometry' in two night frames, and the §8 matrix repeats it - but the spec never says how the builder is allowed to produce them. BUILDER.md's lane rule is 'Only `environment` adds lights', and ARCHITECTURE §12 assigns lamp halos to `props`. The sibling specs all resolve this explicitly - `props.md` supersedes §12's 'real point lights only near camera', `traffic.md` says pools 'are emissive geometry and projected decals, never `PointLight` / `SpotLight`', `transit.md` says the same - so the house convention is that a spec must settle it. audio.md is silent, so the builder guesses: real PointLights (breaks BUILDER.md, and 4+ shadowless lights plus 3 CSM cascades threatens the 34 draw-call ceiling) or faked decals. Four of the sixteen gauntlet frames are night, so the wrong guess is expensive.
gaps.fix: Add one sentence to §3.4, copied from `traffic.md`: 'Lamp pools are emissive geometry and projected ground decals, never `PointLight` / `SpotLight` - only `environment` adds lights. The pool is a decal or a shader term on the ground material, darkened by `(1 - 0.5 * world.weather.night)` like everything else.'

gaps.problem: §3.3 requires `imgstats.mjs` to emit `poolCount`, `poolPx` and `bootFrame`, and items 23 and 25 grade against them - but item 24, which defines every other measurement to the pixel (`stagedPct`, `fogColor`, `horizonRow`, tiling autocorrelation, horizon band, golden hour, noon contrast), never defines what a 'pool' is (8-connected component? ground-only mask? how is 'adjacent to lamp geometry' computed from a PNG?) or what makes a frame a `bootFrame`. Since §3.3 also tells the critic to read the JSON and not the script, and the script lives inside the builder's own blast radius, these two graded numbers are whatever the builder decides they mean. A builder can pass item 23 by counting any bright blob and the critic has been instructed not to look at how.
gaps.fix: Extend item 24 with the same rigour it already applies to `stagedPct`: define a pool as an 8-connected component of non-panel pixels with L >= 110 whose area is >= 350 px and whose centroid lies below the ground/sky boundary, report `poolCount` and the per-pool `poolPx` array, and either drop the 'adjacent to lamp geometry' clause or replace it with a computable proxy (centroid within 120 px of a pixel with L >= 200). Define `bootFrame` explicitly (e.g. `true` iff `p99 < 60` and `stagedPct < 5`), or drop it and rely on item 25's `summary.json` `ok/moduleStatus/panel visible` triple, which is already mechanical.

gaps.problem: §2.3 defines `play(...) -> boolean // true iff audible output was scheduled`, while §3.1 requires that in headless the model, the Poisson scheduler and the virtual voice list all keep running with no audio graph and no audible output. So what does `play` return in a headless frame? The spec never says, and item 14 makes it load-bearing twice: its table asserts `wouldPlay: true` at 10 m while §2.3 says `wouldPlay` is 'exactly what `play` would return', and it asserts 'at 4r+1 the matching `api.play(name, {x, z})` returns `false`' - a check that is vacuous if `play` returns false at every distance in headless. r1's implementation returns `S.mixer ? ... : false`, i.e. false always when disabled, so the default reading breaks item 14.
gaps.fix: Add one sentence to §2.3: 'In headless, `play` returns `true` when it schedules a virtual voice (the model runs; only the graph is absent), so `probeVoice().wouldPlay` and `play`'s return agree in every mode.' And change item 14's 4r+1 clause to grade `api.stats().schedulerEvents` unchanged in addition to the boolean, so the check is non-vacuous whichever mode the critic probes in.

gaps.problem: Item 13 requires `voicesPeak <= 18` and `voicesDropped >= 22` from 'firing 40 one-shots inside 200 ms'. Those two numbers are only simultaneously reachable if no voice completes and frees a slot during the burst - i.e. only if the one-shot used is longer than ~200 ms. The spec never names the sound or a minimum length, and the catalogue is the builder's own, so a correct mixer probed with a 120 ms `ui_click` reports something like `voicesDropped: 15` and fails an item it actually satisfies. `MAX_VOICES = 18` in r1 already matches, so the trap is purely in the probe definition.
gaps.fix: Name the sound and its floor in item 13: 'Firing 40 `siren` one-shots (any catalogue one-shot with `seconds >= 2`) inside 200 ms, with requested volumes spread over 0.05...1.0: ...' and have `liveprobe.mjs` record the sound name it used in `live.json`.

gaps.problem: §3 sets the weighting (60 % soundscape / 25 % panel / 15 % park) but nothing maps the 26-item checklist onto the 0-10 scale, and the only anchors available - CRITIC.md's and CS2-LOOK.md's '10 = indistinguishable from CS2 at that zoom/time' - are meaningless on the 60 % axis, because the critic cannot hear anything and CS2 publishes no `selftest.json` to compare against. If 24 of 26 items pass, is that 8.6 or 7.5? The builder self-scores and the critic scores with no shared anchor on the axis carrying most of the weight. The sibling `simulation.md` at least adds the clarifying sentence that errors/status/budget are gates rather than weights (per §13); audio.md omits even that, so a critic could double-count the triangle overage as both a gate and a score deduction.
gaps.fix: Add three anchor lines under §3 for the 60 % axis, e.g. 'all of items 1-14 pass = 9.0; one whole item failing on a single curve (a rush-hour bump, a cutoff slope) = 7.5; the mix model not steppable in node, or determinism broken = 5.0; no catalogue coverage = 3.' Then copy simulation.md's sentence: 'zero console errors, `status: ready` and the budget are gates, not weighted components - per ARCHITECTURE §13 a pass requires them regardless of score.'

gaps.problem: The spec restates BUILDER.md's writable-file list three separate times (§3.3 in full, item 24 'BUILDER.md does not permit a script committed under `shots/`', item 26 'BUILDER.md forbids both'), restates CRITIC.md's non-visual scoring sentence in §3, and pastes CRITIC.md's `apicheck` launch args plus `tools/screenshot.mjs`'s two-entry `executablePath` array into §3.3 - in the same paragraph that says 'Do not hard-code a Chromium path', while hard-coding the path list. When the Chromium bump the paragraph is guarding against actually happens, this spec is the copy that goes stale, and the builder is following a stale copy that contradicts its own instruction.
gaps.fix: Cut §3.3's code block down to the two deltas that are genuinely audio-specific ('launch exactly as CRITIC.md's `apicheck` block does, with two changes: no `headless=1` in the URL, and `--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required` appended to `args`; resolve `executablePath` the way `tools/screenshot.mjs:28` does rather than hard-coding one') and delete the pasted array. Replace the three blast-radius restatements with a single pointer in §3.3.

gaps.problem: Items 15 and 21 require the beds to move over a 3 s / 6 s window 'at `speed=1`', and item 21 requires the event log to gain a row - but `tools/screenshot.mjs` sets `speed: args.speed ?? '0'`, so every gauntlet frame including the `closeup_12.png` that item 20 is graded from runs with a frozen clock. Item 20(e)'s timeline 'now' marker and (f)'s non-flat VU therefore have to work at `speed=0`, which is only possible because `Clock.advance` still emits `time:tick` with a real `dt` when paused - a subtlety the spec never states while simultaneously banning `performance.now()` in logic. Neither the builder's nor the critic's gauntlet command in the role files passes `--speed`, so the item 15/21 captures do not exist unless someone thinks to add it.
gaps.fix: State it once in §4's preamble: 'the gauntlet runs at `speed=0`; the scheduler and meters must therefore run off the `dt` carried by `time:tick`, which the clock emits even when paused. Items 15 and 21 are the two that require `--speed 1`; shoot them explicitly as `panel_12_speed1_a/b.png` 6 s apart.'

gaps.problem: Item 8's hour sweep is pinned at `rain = 0, temperature = 18`, but two of its cricket clauses are stated at off-sweep inputs ('= 0 at `temperature <= 5`', '<= 0.15 x max at `rain >= 0.6`') without saying at which hour they are evaluated or which run 'max' refers to - the rain-0 sweep maximum, or the maximum of the rain-0.6 run. A builder normalising against the wet run passes trivially; a critic reading it against the dry run fails a correct module.
gaps.fix: Pin them: 'evaluated at hour 01:00 with the sweep's other inputs unchanged; `max` always means the maximum over the pinned rain = 0, temperature = 18 hour sweep.'

gaps.problem: §3.1 reinterprets ARCHITECTURE §12's 'disabled in headless' to mean only 'no AudioContext and no audible output', instructs the critic not to read the difference as a violation, and states that this 'needs no `docs/core-requests/audio.md` entry'. The reasoning is sound and item 15 pins the observable meaning unambiguously, so the damage is small - but a module spec unilaterally narrowing a clause of the contract is exactly what the core-request channel exists for, and §12 is the document the critic is told to calibrate against first.
gaps.fix: Either file the one-line §12 clarification as `docs/core-requests/audio.md` and have §3.1 cite it, or keep the prose and add 'record this reading in `docs/builds/audio_r2.json` under `assumptions` so the integrator can fold it into §12' - so the reinterpretation is on the record rather than only in the spec that benefits from it.

strengths: Factual accuracy is exceptional and I verified it rather than trusting it: `tools/screenshot.mjs` really appends `headless=1` and really resolves `executablePath` from that two-path list; `src/modules/audio/index.js:55-70` really is the positional law quoted; `index.js:261` really accepts only `{traffic}`; `mixer.js:102-107` really is the quietest-voice eviction policy and `MAX_VOICES = 18` matches the §5 budget; `shots/audio/r1/summary.json` really reports 996288 triangles / 42 draw calls; `shots/audio/r1/imgstats.json` really reports closeup_22 mean 56.2 and closeup_12 `bootFrame: true`; `shots/audio/r1/aerial_6p5.json` really carries exactly the two Vite `requestfailed` warnings item 26 excludes. Nothing in the spec's evidence base is invented.

The arithmetic is exact, which is what makes items 7-9 gradable: 24/0.05+1 = 481, 481x16 = 7696, and all sixteen entries of the distance table reproduce `40*35^(k/15)` to the printed decimal. Pinning `gridPoints: 7696` and `distanceSteps` in the JSON so the critic checks two integers instead of reconstructing a grid is a genuinely good device.

Item 14's worked numbers are correct to six decimals against the quoted formula (10 m -> 0.985346 / -0.071407; 300 m -> 0.069517 / -0.800000 clamped; 4r+1 = 329), so a builder can unit-test the law before shooting anything.

World data is handled better than 'copied': §2 correctly states that ARCHITECTURE §3 defines no audio section and forbids writing `world` at all, §2.1 copies the §5 rows verbatim, and it separates the two events (`services:changed`, `sim:milestone`) that are NOT in §5 into their own table sourced from the owning specs - then flags that §15 and `simulation.md` disagree on `sim:milestone` and explains why the disagreement cannot bite. That is the right handling of a real inconsistency.

Every dependency API I spot-checked exists with the stated shape: `rng.float/range/int/bool/pick/weighted/gauss/shuffle/fork`, `events.on/once/off/offOwner/emit/listenerCount`, `camera.apply/registerPreset/flyTo/enableControls/screenToGround`, `assets.procedural.solid/noiseTexture/gradient/noiseNormal`, `engine.onBeforeRender/onAfterRender/stats`, `environment.setupMaterial/hookScene`, `__sim.stats().moduleMs`/`heapMB`, `registry.status().<m>.initMs`, `__sim.registry.apis.<m>`. The `Clock` invocation in item 8 matches the real `constructor(world, events)` and `sunElevation(hour)` signature and would actually run in plain node.

The two panel references are correctly identified - I read them. `cs2_5.jpg` is the citizen info panel with uppercase letter-spaced grey labels left, right-aligned values, hairline dividers, cyan accent and a green status chip; `cs2_7.jpg` is the INDUSTRIAL map legend with named colour-swatch rows, Low/High gradient bars and a checkbox column. The spec's descriptions are what is actually in the frames, so the visual target is anchored rather than gestured at.

Known failure modes are all project-specific and traceable (r1's dead panel, milky night, over-budget declaration, boot frame, 24 kHz, the setAudio machine gun) or attributed to the neighbour that paid for them (tiling -> terrain/simulation r1, razor horizon -> environment r2, blown golden hour -> effects r1, 720p clipping -> ui r1) - and those critic reports exist on disk.

Blast radius is enforced with more care than the role file requires: it notices that r1's `imgstats.mjs` was committed under `shots/`, which BUILDER.md does not permit, and relocates all three probe scripts into `src/modules/audio/` with only their output under `shots/`.

Budget is internally consistent and strictly inside ARCHITECTURE §9 on every axis (0.30/0.8 ms vs the 2 ms per-module ceiling, 420k tri vs 3M, 2.0 s of the 15 s init, 2 MB growth vs 512 MB heap), and `constants.BUDGET.perModuleDrawCalls.audio` really is 0 as §5 claims.
verdict: 8.0 - fail (pass is 8.5). All ten properties are present and the numeric density is the highest I have seen in this repo: I recomputed the 16-step distance table, the 481x16 = 7696 grid and all six of item 14's expected volume/pan values and they are exact; I checked every dependency API named in §7 and every one exists with the stated shape, including the `Clock(world, events).sunElevation(hour)` call that has to run in plain node; I opened cs2_5 and cs2_7 and they are exactly the panels §3.2 says they are; and every r1 number cited (996288 triangles, 42 draw calls, mean 56.2, `bootFrame: true`, the two Vite `requestfailed` warnings in `aerial_6p5.json`, `MAX_VOICES = 18`, the `index.js:55-70` law, the `index.js:261` traffic-only hint) is real. §2 handles world data better than the standard asks, correctly reporting that ARCHITECTURE §3 defines no audio section and separating the two events that §5 does not own. That is 8-plus work. What holds it below the bar is not vagueness but four collisions that a builder cannot resolve without guessing, each of which can cost one of the four remaining rounds. Item 14 hard-codes expected pan values derived from `bandstand`'s yaw and distance while §8 explicitly permits retuning those same numbers - the two instructions cannot both be obeyed. Item 23 demands night lamp pools while BUILDER.md forbids this builder from adding lights and, unlike `props.md`, `traffic.md` and `transit.md`, this spec never says the pools must be emissive geometry and decals. `poolCount`, `poolPx` and `bootFrame` are graded numbers with no definition, produced by a script inside the builder's blast radius that the critic is instructed not to read - while `stagedPct` beside them is defined to the pixel, which shows the author knew the standard and simply missed three fields. And `play`'s return value in headless is undefined in a spec whose central change is running the whole model headless, which makes item 14's `wouldPlay` clause self-contradictory. On the critic lens, roughly 20 of 26 items are mechanically gradable from JSON, which is good; the arguments live in item 20's nine by-eye sub-items (including telling a spectrogram from a waveform at 96x18 px), item 23's undefined pools, item 25's planting judgement and item 19's 'nothing clips'. Fix gaps 1-4 and this is comfortably a 9.
